title: CVE-2023-28319: UAF in SSH sha256 fingerprint check
excerpt:
## Summary:
The fingerprint_b64 pointer is as parameter for failure logging after it is freed.

## Steps To Reproduce:
1. git clone https://github.com/curl/curl
2. vim curl/lib/vssh/libssh2.c
3. search for the string 'free(fingerprint_b64)' and note that fingerprint_b64 is used as parameter immediately after it is freed.

## Supporting Material/References:
The following are the details of the code.

git commit a51f90ec0f74176776f5d14b99689f9241660eaa (HEAD -> master, origin/master, origin/HEAD)

In curl/lib/vssh/libssh2.c
 653 static CURLcode ssh_check_fingerprint(struct Curl_easy *data)
 654 {
 ...
 667     char *fingerprint_b64 = NULL;
 ...
 729     if((pub_pos != b64_pos) ||
 730        strncmp(fingerprint_b64, pubkey_sha256, pub_pos)) {
 731       free(fingerprint_b64);
 732 
 733       failf(data,
 734             "Denied establishing ssh session: mismatch sha256 fingerprint. "
 735             "Remote %s is not equal to %s", fingerprint_b64, pubkey_sha256);

According to git blame, the following commits were involved:

d1e7d9197b lib/vssh/libssh2.c (Mats Lindestam          2021-09-26 23:20:53 +0200  731)       free(fingerprint_b64);
d1e7d9197b lib/vssh/libssh2.c (Mats Lindestam          2021-09-26 23:20:53 +0200  732) 
d1e7d9197b lib/vssh/libssh2.c (Mats Lindestam          2021-09-26 23:20:53 +0200  733)       failf(data,
ff2f3e8367 lib/vssh/libssh2.c (Daniel Stenberg         2022-04-25 11:41:20 +0200  734)             "Denied establishing ssh session: mismatch sha256 fingerprint. "
ff2f3e8367 lib/vssh/libssh2.c (Daniel Stenberg         2022-04-25 11:41:20 +0200  735)             "Remote %s is not equal to %s", fingerprint_b64, pubkey_sha256);

## Impact

Depends on which memory is the pointer fingerprint_b64 pointing to at the time failf() is called, it may either crash the application or it may print out whatever was in memory at the time leading to information leak in the fail log.

summary: The report claims that curl has a use-after-free vulnerability in the SSH fingerprint check function where a pointer is used after being freed, leading to potential crashes or information leaks.

claims.text: The pointer fingerprint_b64 is used as a parameter to failf() after it has been freed
claims.reasoning: The code at lines 731-735 shows fingerprint_b64 is freed at line 731 and then used as a format argument to failf() at line 735, confirming the use-after-free.

citations.note: fingerprint_b64 passed to failf() after free

claims.reasoning: The location matches exactly: ssh_check_fingerprint function in lib/vssh/libssh2.c at lines 731-735.

claims.text: When a SSH server sends a malformed fingerprint or when fingerprint comparison fails
claims.reasoning: The bug triggers when the SSH hostkey fingerprint comparison fails (pub_pos != b64_pos or strncmp mismatch), which an attacker can influence by controlling the server's hostkey or the configured expected fingerprint.

strncmp comparison failure leads to free+use

claims.text: Potential application crash or information leak through fail log exposing freed memory contents
claims.reasoning: Use-after-free can cause crash (DoS) or information leak via the fail log when failf() dereferences the freed pointer to format the error message.

citations.note: freed pointer passed to failf() for logging

claims.text: Clone curl repository, modify lib/vssh/libssh2.c to free fingerprint_b64 and then use it in failf()
claims.reasoning: The bug is reproducible by configuring an expected SHA256 fingerprint that doesn't match the server's actual hostkey, causing the mismatch branch to execute.

citations.note: Trigger condition reachable via SSH server fingerprint mismatch
Bug reproduces when mismatch condition is met

key_reasons: Code at lib/vssh/libssh2.c lines 731-735 shows a clear use-after-free: fingerprint_b64 is freed then passed to failf()
The bug is reachable by an attacker controlling the SSH server's hostkey or the client's expected fingerprint configuration
Impact includes potential crash (denial of service) or information leak via the error log
No project policy excludes this class of bug
reply: Thank you for the report. The use-after-free at lib/vssh/libssh2.c:731-735 is confirmed: fingerprint_b64 is freed then used in the failf() call. This is reachable when the SHA256 fingerprint mismatch check fails, which an attacker can trigger via the server's hostkey or the configured expected fingerprint. The fix should save the fingerprint string before freeing it, or reorder the free after the log call.
